subject: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification — FinLytics / post-call recap
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Alex Carter <alex.carter@finlytics.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-18T15:02:00Z
Subject: Recap & next steps — dedicated capacity sizing/pricing

Alex — great to meet today. Quick recap from our discovery and the items we agreed to validate so we can put a formal dedicated capacity estimate together: 

Summary of FinLytics requirements (as discussed):
- Model: in-house 70B parameter model (quantized 4/8-bit) for document analysis and summarization.
- Avg tokens per request: ~600 tokens (prompt + response).
- Monthly volume (initial): 80M–150M tokens/month; 12-month growth plan to ~500M tokens/month.
- Traffic profile: baseline ~10 RPS, peak ~25 RPS; target latency SLO: p95 < 400ms for short responses (~250 tokens).
- Throughput targets: sustained ~6k tokens/sec, peak bursts up to ~15k tokens/sec.

Cost/contract expectations you mentioned: budget range $20k–$60k/month for a dedicated reserved instance, and a target unit-econ of roughly $120–$250 / 1M tokens (we'll validate mappings).

Open questions for your team (so we can finalize sizing/pricing):
1) Are you planning to run any synchronous low-latency endpoints (<200ms) vs mostly async/batch?
2) Will model weights be hosted by Redwood or do you need an air-gapped/private deployment?
3) Any hard limits on inference windows (e.g., 99th pct concurrent requests)?

Next steps (proposed):
- Internal: Marissa to send a baseline dedicated estimate with GPU options (H100 vs A100) and mapped unit-econ.
- Technical: Marcus to provide throughput / GPU mapping and any latency caveats for your model shape.
- Customer: Alex to confirm procurement contact and timeline; if numbers align, we’ll prepare a SOW + reserved capacity contract.

I’ll loop back once Marissa shares the estimate. Thanks — appreciate the context, and great fit for a dedicated deployment given predictable volume and latency needs.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132
From: Alex Carter <alex.carter@finlytics.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@finlytics.ai>
Date: 2027-06-18T18:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — dedicated capacity sizing/pricing

Thanks Dylan — that matches our notes from the call. A few clarifications: 
- We'll primarily be serving synchronous APIs (customer-facing features) with tight p95 SLAs on shorter responses; occasional async batches for large backfills.
- We intend to host model weights centrally (not air-gapped) but need KMS integration and audit logs.
- Procurement timeline: aiming to finalize budget and vendor by end of Q3; procurement point of contact is Procurement <procurement@finlytics.ai>.

Budget flexibility: we can stretch to ~$65k/month if the unit economics hit the $150 / 1M token mark with guaranteed throughput.

If you can get a ballpark estimate with GPU options and monthly reserved costs, we can fast-track an internal approval.

Alex Carter
Head of AI Product, FinLytics
alex.carter@finlytics.ai | +1 (212) 555-0194
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Carter <alex.carter@finlytics.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-19T01:22:00Z
Subject: Redwood dedicated estimate — FinLytics (initial)

Alex / Dylan — attaching an initial estimate and mapping workbook (FinLytics-MAP.xlsx) for your review — see attached. High level: 

Options (monthly reserved pricing, list):
1) 2x NVIDIA H100 (reserved) — $45,000 / month (recommended)
   - Typical throughput: sustained ~6k tokens/sec per 2x H100 for your quantized 70B setup; peak burst handling ~15k tokens/sec with autoscaling/burst pool.
   - Unit-econ mapping (approx): $160 / 1M tokens at 150M tokens/month; improves to ~$120 / 1M at 500M tokens/mo with amortization/efficiencies.

2) 4x NVIDIA A100 80GB (reserved) — $55,000 / month
   - Higher concurrency for many short requests; similar or slightly higher $/1M token vs H100 depending on batch efficiency.

3) Dedicated shared CPU cache + prefix caching optimizations can reduce effective token usage by 10–20% for repeated prompts (we can instrument after onboarding).

Notes / assumptions:
- Pricing above is for a Dedicated capacity reservation (SLA-backed). Includes base support and 30-day rolling kernel updates.
- KMS integration and audit logs available as add-on (pricing in attached PDF).
- We modeled average tokens/request = 600, 150M tokens baseline for the initial price point; we’ll re-run the workbook for other volume bands.

Deliverables if you move forward: formal SOW, capacity sizing diagram, and a technical onboarding session to validate latency across your full prompt mix.

Attachments: Redwood-Dedicated-Estimate-FinLytics.pdf, FinLytics-MAP.xlsx

Happy to hop on a quick call to walk through the workbook tomorrow if helpful.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sales Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0177
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Carter <alex.carter@finlytics.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-19T03:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Redwood dedicated estimate — FinLytics (throughput mapping)

Alex / team — quick technical note to augment Marissa’s estimate with throughput/latency guidance: 

- Model shape and quantization matter: assuming 8-bit or 4-bit quantization and optimized kernels, 2x H100 hits the target sustained ~6k tokens/sec and p95 latency ~300–400ms for ~250-token responses.
- If you need p95 <200ms for 250-token responses, we'd recommend 4x A100 (or additional H100 capacity) to reduce queuing and give headroom for concurrency.
- Bottlenecks to watch: KV cache size (large context windows), and any synchronous preprocessing steps. We recommend enabling prefix caching for repeated request patterns — that often reduces effective tokens per call by ~10–20%.

Operational notes:
- Autoscaling/burst pool: Redwood can burst to extra capacity for short windows (subject to pool availability); include burst credits in the SOW if you have predictable spikes.
- Fallbacks: we can configure a smaller/cheaper model for non-critical paths to reduce unit costs.

If you send sample prompt set + token histogram, I’ll run a short perf test on our internal runners and return a calibrated latency/throughput spreadsheet.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Lead Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference

1) Marissa will finalize a formal estimate (PDF + workbook) today with the two recommended configurations (2x H100 & 4x A100), include KMS addon pricing and burst-credit options.
2) Marcus will do a short perf-run if you can share a representative prompt set + token histogram (Marcus will provide upload instructions).
3) If pricing aligns with your budget (~$45k–$60k/mo target), Procurement can expect a SOW + reserved capacity contract for signature within 7 business days of acceptance.

Can Procurement confirm preferred contract owner (FinLytics, Inc.) and any required PO/terms up front? Also, Alex — are you available for a 30 min technical kickoff Wednesday at 10am PT? If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite and attach the draft estimate.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.
